name: port-whitelist
description: Port whitelist: only 53, 80 and 443 (TCP and UDP) leave the client's network; everything else is silently dropped, whatever it contains. Only the families that live on 443 survive.
analogue: Iran's crisis-mode whitelister as first described by Bock et al. (FOCI 2020) and seen in the June 2025 'stealth blackout': DNS/53, HTTP/80 and HTTPS/443 forwarded, everything else dropped without RST or ICMP. Model: destination PORT only — it does not look at what the flow carries (protocol-whitelist does), and it still lets UDP/443 through, which the 2025–26 posture no longer does.
